last_cycle_outcome: H66 KILLED at the PROTOTYPE rung. ASYM gradient KICK as a TERMINAL stage (perturb-and-repair with a gradient-guided destroy operator). NOTHING PROMOTED - sota.json untouched. THE MECHANISM IS REAL AND IT HAS EXPIRED, and that pair is the result. POSITIVE CONTROL on H35's 83.91351804242117 order: best arm 83.93365540548263 = +0.020137 pp vs base, +0.018620 pp attributable against a no-kick control of 83.91503550248125, 7/12 arms positive - which independently reproduces backlog.md:2119's logged +0.0179 pp for the same mechanism on the 83.9035 MPS-era base to within 0.0007 pp. So the harness is validated and the null below is not an implementation defect. ON THE H64 CHAMPION (84.25817950936937) the same code and the same grid give EXACTLY +0.000000 pp on all 18 arms (reach 414/2000/20000 x displacement 0.25/1/4 ranks x repair 2/8 sweeps, 150 steps); the best raw repair is 84.23740032750892, i.e. 0.020779 pp BELOW its own input - perturb-and-repair does not get back to where it started. TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS EXPLAIN IT. (1) The M12 control - champion order + the same repair sift, NO kick - has EXACTLY 0.000000 pp of headroom (vs +0.001517 pp on the weak base), so there is no ground left for this class to take, and the M8 redundancy fraction is UNDEFINED because both terms are 0. (2) The champion order is a STRICT LOCAL MAXIMUM of the discrete score along the ASYM gradient: the first node-moving step already loses 0.041754-0.159932 pp and the trajectory is monotone down to -1.189355 pp; not one of ~900 logged (arm, step) points is above the champion. NOT a reach problem - at reach 414 the champion has 10.43% of backward weight live vs the weak base's 2.15% and still gains nothing. NO SCREEN WAS RUN and that is not a shortcut: H66 is a PURE TERMINAL APPEND, and M12's 2026-08-26 amendment says a from-champion prototype is a genuine PREDICTION for a pure append (measured on H59 at 0.35% relative error). So the prototype predicts the screen at +0.000000 pp; that prediction is recorded in log.md so that running it and getting something else would falsify M12's amendment. A TEST FLAW WAS FOUND AND FIXED MID-CYCLE: rungs 1-2 sifted from the BEST-BY-ORACLE rank, which is the unperturbed champion order, so they reproduced the control by construction and never tested repair at all; the item's own prior evidence (backlog.md:2090-2130) is what revealed it. NEW META-RULE M13-perturb-repair-gains-expire: a perturb-and-repair gain measured on an older, weaker base does NOT transfer and must be re-measured on the sitting champion; the cheap diagnostic is to run the repair operator ALONE from the champion order and read its headroom. M13 is the sibling of M12 - M12 is about a MIS-SITED measurement, M13 about an OUT-OF-DATE one. PROCESS NOTE: the critic rung was not run, per the ladder for a prototype kill (precedent cycles 10/11/12); the adversarial work a critic would have demanded is the positive control, which rules out the single most likely way this kill could be wrong. P23 WAS CHECKED FIRST as cycle 18 instructed and is STILL awaiting-operator - HEAD was 3d79b71 with no ruling on the branch - so H74 and H70's score leg stay blocked and this cycle took the unblocked connectome axis. New items H75 and P25 (apply M13 to the standing queue; record which base a prior_evidence delta came from).

_escalation_note: cycles_since_score_move is the PRIMARY divergence trigger as of 2026-08-15 (campaign.yaml escalation.divergent_after_k_cycles_without_score_move: 3). Increment it at the end of EVERY cycle regardless of verdict; reset to 0 only on a champion change. It replaces consecutive_kills as the primary trigger because that counter never left 0 in 7 cycles - 4 of them were infrastructure items, which by construction never increment it, and both science items passed. At 3 the campaign is FORCED out of incremental mode and an infrastructure item no longer satisfies the requirement.
